title: Ramps: Building Bent-Line Graphs from ReLU
short: ReLU(x) = max(0, x) is a ramp; sums of shifted, scaled ramps make any bent-line graph.
trouble: Students read ReLU(x − 3) as bending at x = −3, or use the new slope as a ramp's coefficient when the coefficient is the change in slope at the bend.

blocks.html: You already know two kinds of bent graphs: the V of the absolute value function and the pieces of a piecewise function. Both can be built from one simple shape, the ramp: $$\operatorname{ReLU}(x) = \max(0, x) = \begin{cases} 0, & x < 0 \\ x, & x \ge 0. \end{cases}$$ It is flat at $0$ for negative inputs, then rises with slope $1$. (ReLU is short for "rectified linear unit.")

A shifted, scaled ramp $c\operatorname{ReLU}(x - a)$ is $0$ to the left of $x = a$ and a line of slope $c$ to the right of it. Add a few ramps (and a line) and you get a bent-line graph. Each ramp makes one bend, at its $a$, and its coefficient $c$ is how much the slope changes there.

To the left of $a$, the inside $x - a$ is negative, so the ramp adds $0$ and the graph is unchanged there. To the right of $a$, the ramp adds $c(x - a)$, a line with slope $c$. When you add functions, heights add, so slopes add too: past the bend, the new slope is the old slope plus $c$. The shift works like any transformation: $\operatorname{ReLU}(x - 3)$ is the ramp moved $3$ units right, and $\operatorname{ReLU}(-x)$ is the ramp reflected across the $y$-axis.

blocks.name: alg2-ramps
blocks.cap: Two ramps: $\operatorname{ReLU}(x)$ opens to the right and $\operatorname{ReLU}(-x)$ opens to the left. Their sum (blue) is $|x|$. Drag a bend, change a coefficient or add a ramp.

blocks.title: Absolute value from two ramps
steps: For $x \ge 0$: $\operatorname{ReLU}(x) = x$, and $-x \le 0$ gives $\operatorname{ReLU}(-x) = 0$. The sum is $x$, which is $|x|$.
For $x < 0$: $\operatorname{ReLU}(x) = 0$, and $-x$ is positive, so $\operatorname{ReLU}(-x) = -x$. The sum is $-x$, which is $|x|$.

blocks.title: Reading a sum of ramps
blocks.q: Let $f(x) = 2\operatorname{ReLU}(x + 1) - 3\operatorname{ReLU}(x - 2)$. Find $f(4)$ and the slope of each straight piece.
steps: At $x = 4$ the insides are $4 + 1 = 5$ and $4 - 2 = 2$, both positive. So $f(4) = 2 \cdot 5 - 3 \cdot 2 = 4$.
The bends are where the insides are $0$: $x = -1$ and $x = 2$.
Slopes: $0$ to the left of $-1$; $0 + 2 = 2$ between $-1$ and $2$; $2 + (-3) = -1$ to the right of $2$.

blocks.title: Writing a graph as ramps
blocks.q: A graph comes down with slope $-1$ until the point $(0, 1)$, rises with slope $1$ until $(3, 4)$, and then stays flat. Write it with ramps.
steps: Start with the line of the left piece: slope $-1$ through $(0, 1)$ is $y = -x + 1$.
At $x = 0$ the slope changes from $-1$ to $1$, a change of $2$. Add $2\operatorname{ReLU}(x)$.
At $x = 3$ the slope changes from $1$ to $0$, a change of $-1$. Add $-\operatorname{ReLU}(x - 3)$.
Check $x = 5$: $-5 + 1 + 2 \cdot 5 - 2 = 4$, the height of the flat piece. ✓

blocks.name: alg2-ramps

opts.task: Make the blue graph land on the gold one from the last example. The line $-x + 1$ is already there; set the two ramps.

blocks.cap: Drag the bends sideways and set each coefficient to the change in slope at its bend.

blocks.html: Shifting the wrong way. $\operatorname{ReLU}(x - 3)$ bends at $x = 3$, not at $x = -3$. Find each bend by setting the inside equal to $0$. Check: put your bend into the inside; you should get $0$.

Using the new slope as the coefficient. In the last example it is tempting to write $1 \cdot \operatorname{ReLU}(x)$, because the slope after $0$ is $1$. But a ramp adds its coefficient to the slope already there, so that would give $-1 + 1 = 0$, a flat piece. Check: add up the coefficients from the left to get each piece's slope, and compare with the graph.

Ramps are the building blocks of many neural networks, the math inside much of today's speech and image recognition. A network adds up many shifted, scaled ramps, just as you did here. You will meet one in Linear Algebra.
